questions.question: Should CoS always run context-builder first?
questions.answer: ChiefOfStaff decides - it IS the brain
questions.insight: Agents are STUPID TOOLS that execute predetermined workflows. ChiefOfStaff is the REASONING BRAIN. CoS decides what context each agent needs, how to use embeddings, etc. All operations need context - CoS determines WHICH context.

questions.question: Can CoS run multiple agents in parallel?
questions.answer: Yes - parallel, sequential, or DAG pipelines
questions.insight: ChiefOfStaff can orchestrate agents in ANY pattern: parallel, sequential, or complex DAGs. It depends on the task and context. For empty note classification, CoS might call multiple experts (vault context, recent actions, links) before deciding.

questions.question: How should CoS synthesize results for InsightStream?
Should CoS have memory of recent tasks?

analysis: CRITICAL INSIGHT: ChiefOfStaff is an AUTONOMOUS BACKGROUND AGENT. It receives signals, reasons, triggers agents (possibly in parallel/DAG), processes results, and may trigger MORE agents until satisfied. Only then does it present to human. Agents are 'stupid tools' - CoS is the brain. Each agent can make multiple LLM rounds internally. This is the 'sentient note' vision.
keyInsights: ChiefOfStaff = reasoning brain, autonomous background agent
CoS decides context, triggers agents, processes results, may loop
Execution can be parallel, sequential, or DAG-based
CoS keeps reasoning until satisfied to present to human
This makes notes 'sentient' - intelligence depends on note complexity
